extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, meteorologists, geographers, and educated readers of 19th-century natural history
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and interpretive principles for observing and describing atmospheric electricity, weather phenomena, and the geographical distribution of plants and animals; includes instrument-scoped recommendations, sampling strategies, and correlations between climate lines and species distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electrometric observation reporting criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Limiting itself to results yielded by electrometric observations... the physical description of the universe should merely notice the incontestable increase of intensity in the general positive electricity of the atmosphere accompanying an increase of altitude and the absence of trees, its daily variations (which, according to Clark's experiments at Dublin, take place at more complicated periods than those found by Saussure and myself), and its variations in the different seasons of the year, at different distances from the equator, and in the different relations of continental or oceanic surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting electrometric results, record (a) the relation of positive electricity intensity with altitude and vegetation cover, (b) daily variation patterns (noting differing periodicities observed by different investigators), and (c) seasonal, latitudinal, and continental versus oceanic differences. Cite comparative experiments (e.g., Clark, Saussure) for period characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electrometer experimental controls
rubrics_metrics.description: I here only refer to those of my experiments in which the three-foot metallic conductor of Saussure's electrometer was neither moved upward nor downward, nor, according to Volta's proposal, armed with burning sponge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude or separately note results from experiments in which the apparatus was altered (e.g., moving the conductor or adding burning sponge). Maintain consistent apparatus configuration to ensure comparability and to avoid confounding factors known in 'quaestiones vexatae' of atmospheric electricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface-type influence on electric equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: The electric equilibrium is less frequently disturbed where the aerial ocean rests on a liquid base than where it impends over the land; and it is very striking to observe how, in extensive seas, small insular groups affect the condition of the atmosphere, and occasion the formation of storms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In analyses of atmospheric electricity and storm formation, explicitly account for whether the atmosphere overlies oceanic or continental surfaces and for the presence of islands; expect greater disturbance over land and localized effects from insular groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fog and precipitation effects on atmospheric polarity
rubrics_metrics.description: In fogs, and in the commencement of falls of snow, I have seen... the previously permanent positive electricity rapidly pass into the negative condition... The alternate transition was precisely similar to that indicated by the electrometer shortly before and during a storm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor polarity during fog formation and early precipitation; rapid transitions from positive to negative can precede storms and should be recorded as diagnostic temporal markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cloud charging and visible-color correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the vesicles of vapor have become condensed into clouds, having definite outlines, the electric tension of the external surface will be increased in proportion to the amount of electricity which passes over to it from the separate vesicles of vapor... Slate-gray clouds are charged, according to Peltier's experiments at Paris, with negative, and white, red, and orange-colored clouds with positive electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate cloud morphology and visible color to electric tension: note cloud outline definition and color as potential indicators of sign and magnitude of charge, while acknowledging discordant views among investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of lightning phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Arago's investigations... the evolution of light (lightning) is of three kinds -- zigzag, and sharply defined at the edges; in sheets of light, illuminating a whole cloud; and in the form of fire-balls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing lightning, classify occurrences into Arago's three types (zigzag, sheet illumination, globular/fire-ball) and record duration (the first two extremely brief; globular often visible for several seconds) and whether luminous precipitation or luminous clouds occur without audible thunder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution of storms as observational datum
rubrics_metrics.description: In the geographical distribution of storms, the Peruvian coast, which is not visited by thunder or lightning, presents the most striking contrast to the rest of the tropical zone... electric explosions are extremely rare in high northern regions (between 70 degrees and 75 degrees latitude).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include regional contrasts in storm frequency (e.g., Peruvian coast vs. other tropics, polar latitudes) as part of meteorological description; use navigators' testimonies and compiled observations to establish geographic patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental scope for atmospheric measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been justly remarked, that it is the barometer alone which indicates to us the changes that occur in the pressure of the air throughout all the aerial strata from the place of observation to the extremest confines of the atmosphere, while the thermometer and psychrometer only acquaint us with all the variations occurring in the local heat and moisture of the lower strata of air in contact with the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the barometer to infer pressure changes through the full column of air; treat thermometer and hygrometric instruments as measurements primarily of the lower atmospheric strata in contact with the surface. Do not substitute local thermometric readings for columnar pressure inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferential methods for upper-atmosphere thermic/hygrometric state
rubrics_metrics.description: The simultaneous thermic and hygrometric modifications of the upper regions of the air can only be learned (when direct observations on mountain stations or aerostatic ascents are impracticable) from hypothetical combinations, by making the barometer serve both as a thermometer and an hygrometer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When direct upper-air observations are impossible, construct hypothetical combinations using barometric data to infer temperature and humidity aloft, but label such inferences as hypothetical and conditional on assumptions; prioritize direct mountain or aerostatic measurements when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretative principle for causation of important weather changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Important changes of weather are not owing to merely local causes, situated at the place of observation, but are the consequence of a disturbance in the equilibrium of the aerial currents at a great distance from the surface of the Earth, in the higher strata of the atmosphere...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In explanations of significant weather changes, emphasize remote upper-air disturbances and large-scale aerial-current equilibrium shifts rather than attributing changes solely to local surface phenomena. Use synoptic perspective where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic focus recommendation for meteorological progress
rubrics_metrics.description: It has always appeared to me that meteorology must first seek its foundation and progress in the torrid zone, where the variations of the atmospheric pressure, the course of hydro-meteors, and the phenomena of electric explosion, are all of periodic occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize systematic observations in the torrid (tropical) zone to establish foundational meteorological laws, since many key atmospheric phenomena are periodic and pronounced there; use tropical periodicity to develop general principles applicable elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approaches to studying geographic distribution of organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Vital organisms... may be considered either according to the difference and relative numbers of the types (their arrangement into genera and species), or according to the number of individuals of each species on a given area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying biogeography, adopt either taxonomic-compositional approaches (diversity and relationships among genera and species) or quantitative abundance-based approaches (individual counts per area), and make explicit which approach is used for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of plant distribution: social vs isolated species
rubrics_metrics.description: In the mode of life of plants as in that of animals, an important difference is noticed; they either exist in an isolated state, or live in a social condition. Those species of plants which I have termed 'social' uniformly cover vast extents of land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify plant species as 'social' (forming extensive, uniform cover) or 'isolated'; consider the sociality of a species when interpreting landscape physiognomy and when assessing human impacts such as agriculture, which tend to increase social plant predominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of climatic lines and elevation-latitude comparisons in biogeography
rubrics_metrics.description: The curves of the isothermal lines, and more especially those of the isochimenal lines, correspond with the limits which are seldom passed by certain species of plants, and of animals which do not wander far from their fixed habitation either with respect to elevation or latitude... zones of elevation on mountains correspond to parallels of latitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ isothermal and isochimenal maps and compare elevational belts with latitudinal parallels to delimit species' ranges; use numerical estimates of families' representation as one recedes from the equator, and distinguish 'representative species' (analogous types) from truly identical species when interpreting patterns—consider hypotheses of transport or historical events for anomalous identical occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative elevation-latitude sampling method
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers who in short periods of time have passed over vast tracts of land, and ascended lofty mountains, in which climates were ranged, as it were in strata one above another, must have been early impressed by the regularity with which vegetable forms are distributed... He ingeniously compared the Alpine flora with the flora of plains situated in different latitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample along elevational transects and across latitudinal gradients to compare 'zones' of vegetation; use mountain ascents to observe how climatic belts replicate latitudinal changes and to support generalizations about distribution regularity.
